structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: This letter from Coal India Limited to stock exchanges announces the AGM Notice and Integrated Annual Report including BRSR for FY 2024-25, scheduled for August 28, 2025 via VC/OAVM. It details the electronic distribution of the annual report, availability on the company website and e-voting portal, and procedures for email/bank updates, e-voting, and AGM attendance. It recommends a final dividend of Rs. 5.15 per share with a record date of August 21, 2025, and states payment within 30 days of AGM approval. It mandates submission of tax documents (Forms 15G/15H, PAN, tax residency certificates, Rule 37BA documents) through a designated tax portal open August 27 to September 3, 2025, with email fallback, and warns of higher TDS for non-compliance. It also sets August 21, 2025 as the cut-off date for voting eligibility.

nodes.title: From Aspiration to Achievement — Viksit Bharat in Sight
nodes.summary: The text discusses India's aspiration to become a developed nation (Viksit Bharat) by 2047, emphasizing energy needs. It highlights India's $4 trillion economy, low per capita electricity demand, and growing energy demand. Coal remains dominant despite renewable focus. The government targets increased domestic coal production and reduced imports. CIL's investments include large equipment, land, transportation infrastructure, a FY26 capex target of ₹16,000 crore, a Net Zero target of 3 GW by FY27-28, and renewable capacity expansion of 6.5 GW by FY29-30. CIL achieved record production of ~781.06 million tonnes in FY24-25, targeting 1 billion tonnes by FY28-29. It is diversifying into critical minerals, renewable energy, coal gasification, pump storage, and thermal power, supported by a strong balance sheet, high credit ratings, and consistent dividends.

nodes.title: Five Decades of Unearthing Energy
nodes.summary: The text celebrates Coal India Limited's (CIL) 50th anniversary in 2025, highlighting its evolution from 79 million tonnes production in 1975 to a record 781.06 million tonnes in 2025, ensuring India's energy security and sustainable future. It details CIL's headquarters in Kolkata, operation under the Ministry of Coal, and lists its ten wholly-owned subsidiaries. It covers the shareholding structure as of March 31, 2025, with the Government of India holding 63.13% and other investors 36.87%. It notes CIL's contribution of ~74% to India's total coal production in FY 2024-25, its 310 mines across eight states in open-cast, underground, and mixed formats, its Maharatna status, and coal's role in nearly 72% of the country's electricity generation.

It includes CIL's vision to be a global energy player ensuring energy security through sustainable growth, and its mission to efficiently produce and market coal in an eco-friendly manner with safety and quality. Additionally, it lists core values: commitment to national energy demand, integrity for stakeholder value, and a learning and innovation-driven culture, referencing a BSE India filing and the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

nodes.title: Year in Perspective
nodes.summary: The text presents Coal India Limited's 2024-25 annual report highlights: financials (net revenue ₹1,43,369 crore, PAT ₹35,302 crore, EPS ₹57.37, dividend ₹26.50/share, 46% payout, AAA rating, EBITDA ₹51,640 crore at 40.68% margin, net worth ₹99,105 crore, market cap ₹2,45,400 crore, balance sheet ₹2,60,198 crore, long-term debt ₹7,386 crore); operational performance (raw coal production 781.06 Mt, offtake 762.98 Mt, 373.5 Mtpa transport capacity via 37 FMC projects); growth highlights (coal-to-chemicals 0.66 Mtpa, coal-to-ammonium-nitrate project, SNG projects, mechanised loading 32%, 87 rakes/day); and ESG & diversification (33 eco-parks, 44 approved, 2,513 lakh KL mine water for 11.8 lakh people in 880 villages, 300 MW solar at ₹2.55/kWh, 9.5 GW renewable target by FY30, 40.38 lakh saplings).

nodes.title: A Value-accretive Growth Model
nodes.summary: The text outlines a value-accretive growth model for Coal India Limited, detailing six capitals: financial (capex, net worth, debt), manufactured (mines, washeries, capacity utilization), natural (solar capacity, treated water, energy), intellectual (R&D investment, testing labs), human (employees, training, recruits), and social/relationship (CSR expenditure). It lists products, the integrated value chain process from exploration to supply chain, risks and opportunities, and materiality. Outputs include financial metrics (revenue, PAT, EPS), operational figures (coal production/offtake, washed coal, solar generation), environmental impacts (CO2 reduction, water recycling, saplings), R&D projects, and employee welfare. Outcomes cover profitability, reliable supply, environmental restoration, productivity, safety, and community well-being, with CSR beneficiaries and exchequer contribution, linked to SDGs.

nodes.title: Focused Initiatives to Amplify Value
key_items: Operational Enhancement; Resource Quality and Infrastructure; Renewable Energy and Sustainability; Innovation and Research
nodes.summary: The text outlines Coal India Limited's structural, operational, and digital initiatives to boost productivity, cut environmental impact, and diversify revenue. It details operational enhancements like rapid-loading silos and mine surveillance; resource quality projects such as washeries; renewable energy installations (solar projects); innovation via a clean coal R&D hub; and governance reforms including GeM contracting, MDO models, and standardized processes. Each initiative's description, resulting value, and linked capitals are provided, highlighting benefits like faster turnaround, cost reduction, and emissions cuts.

nodes.title: The Evolving Landscape of our Operations
key_items: CIL’s response; CIL’s response; CIL’s response
nodes.summary: The text outlines Coal India Limited's evolving operations amid global energy shifts. It covers global supply risks from geopolitics and price volatility; India's accelerated clean energy transition with 50% non-fossil capacity achieved early, raising long-term coal demand concerns; CIL's domestic focus reducing exposure to international freight fluctuations; long-term Fuel Supply Agreements covering ~629 million tonnes/year for power; India's coal resource endowment of 389.421 billion tonnes geological resources, including 212 billion tonnes proven reserves, mostly non-coking (89%) with limited coking coal requiring imports; mine development priorities on high-quality non-coking reserves and joint ventures for coking coal washeries; policy targets of 1.3 billion tonnes by FY2027 and 1.5 billion tonnes by FY2030, commercial mining auctions, mechanized loading and First-Mile Connectivity; and CIL's roadmap targeting 1.23 billion tonnes by FY2035 with 8% annual growth from FY2025, priority railway access, expedited clearances, and diversification into coal gas, CBM, and renewables.

nodes.title: The Evolving Landscape of our Operations (Contd...)
key_items: CIL’s response; CIL’s response; CIL’s response
nodes.summary: The text covers technological upgrades like surface miners, high-wall mining, drones, and automated loading systems for cost-efficiency and safety. Logistics improvements include rail upgrades (Dedicated Freight Corridor, line expansions) and coastal shipping with regulatory support. CIL commissioned 11 new FMC facilities, enhanced loading accuracy, reduced wagon cycle times, and centralized command centres for real-time tracking. New railway sidings and coastal stockyards improved delivery timelines and demand management. Sustainability requirements driven by Net-Zero 2070 and reduced coal share in power by 2030 include lower ash content and stricter mine closure norms. E-auction premiums fell to 48% in FY2025 from 72% due to improved domestic supply and lower international prices. CIL has eight washeries under construction, 209.08 MW solar capacity, fully provisioned mine closure fund, and reclaimed 1,500+ hectares. Auction methodology simplified and bid security lowered to boost participation.

nodes.title: Materiality Assessment Overview
nodes.summary: The text outlines Coal India's materiality assessment and stakeholder engagement approach. It details the FY 2024–25 review process involving cross-departmental input and stakeholder groups, evaluating topics on importance to external stakeholders and business impact. Topics are categorized into Top Priorities (e.g., emissions, community engagement), Hidden Value Creators (e.g., financial performance, energy management), Hygiene Factors (e.g., GHG emissions, land acquisition), and Monitoring Issues (e.g., renewable energy, health & safety), each with key stakeholders and linked capitals. It explains strategic integration through board oversight, investment, ESG-linked KPIs, and communication plans. Additionally, it covers stakeholder engagement philosophy, strategy steps (mapping, categorizing, engaging, responding, monitoring), and the importance of listening to stakeholders for long-term resilience.

nodes.title: Coal India ESG Material Topics: Hygiene, Monitoring, Integration

nodes.title: Stakeholder Insights Empower Our Growth Strategy
nodes.summary: Coal India's stakeholder engagement framework emphasizes listening to diverse groups—customers, investors, government, employees, partners, and communities—to adapt to the energy landscape. Engagement is integrated across the mining lifecycle, from exploration to closure, shaping decisions on risk, investment, and sustainability. The philosophy is structured, transparent, and feedback-driven, aiming to identify concerns early, build trust, and evolve ESG priorities. The strategy includes mapping stakeholder impact, categorizing and prioritizing groups, engaging through dialogue, responding to expectations, and monitoring improvement. Benefits include better decisions, goodwill, minimized disruption, and alignment with GRI, <IR>, BRSR, and UN SDGs. The text details engagement objectives, models, frequency, and KPIs for shareholders, customers, and employees, such as AGMs, analyst meets, consumer meets, grievance portals, union interactions, trainings, and safety programs, with metrics like attendance, resolution rates, satisfaction indices, training hours, injury rates, and attrition.

nodes.title: Engagement Objective

Stakeholders include regulators, suppliers, communities, NGOs, media, and knowledge partners, each with specific objectives like compliance, ethical sourcing, social licence, transparency, and innovation. Engagement methods range from regulatory submissions and vendor systems to CSR outreach, forums, press briefings, and joint studies. Frequencies vary from quarterly to ongoing. KPIs cover compliance breaches, vendor payment cycles, CSR budget utilization, grievance resolution, collaborative programs, media sentiment, and R&D projects. The document also references corporate overview, statutory reports, financial statements, and Coal India Limited's Integrated Annual Report 2024-25.

nodes.title: Governance drives Effective Decision-making

Coal India Limited (CIL) has been steadfast in its commitment to environmental sustainability through extensive afforestation and green belt development.
